queries.title: Is the Stern-Volmer quencher channel an energy-gap-law nonradiative channel?

queries.title: The radiative/nonradiative branching ratio is the energy-gap-law rate ratio
queries.chemicalQuestion: When the nonradiative channel of a two-channel excited state is governed by the energy-gap law, does the quantum-yield branching ratio of the radiative channel equal the EGL rate ratio written through its barrier?
queries.chemicalRationale: QuantumYield is the parallel-channel calculus: `yieldOf k i = k i / sum k`, and its relative-yield law `yieldOf_div_yieldOf` makes a branch ratio a rate ratio. EnergyGapLaw supplies the nonradiative rate `nrRate = A * exp(-nrBarrier/(kB*T))`. Composing them turns a spectroscopic branching observable into the EGL barrier exponential: the statement-level bridge between the yield algebra and the energy-gap law.
